items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Automated guided vehicles (AGVs) are crucial to the advancement of intelligent manufacturing systems. To ensure collision-free navigation for multiple robots in a warehouse environment, this study investigates the impact of time windows on multi-agent path finding and proposes a two-tier planning approach that integrates an enhanced A* algorithm with an effective conflict resolution strategy. In the first tier, to address the issue of excessive node exploration inherent in traditional A* algorithms due to the design of the heuristic function, we introduce a dynamic adjustment of the heuristic weight based on the distance between the current position and the target. This optimization significantly reduces the number of search nodes, thereby improving computational efficiency. Furthermore, a cubic B-spline curve is employed to smooth the generated paths, providing initial collision-free paths for multiple robots. In the second tier, we analyze various types of conflicts, including blocking conflicts, node conflicts, and position conflicts among the robots by utilizing a time-window graph representation of their paths. Based on this analysis, appropriate decoupling strategies are developed to effectively resolve these conflicts. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method successfully generates low-cost, smooth, and collision-free navigation paths for multi-robot systems, thereby improving the overall performance of AGV systems in dynamic environments.</jats:p>
title: A study on multi-warehouse robot path planning with an enhanced A* algorithm considering time window

items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents a general methodology for the off-line planning of optimal trajectory of robot manipulators by taking into account the grasping forces in the manipulator gripper. The mechanical energy of the actuators has been considered for the formulation of the objective function. The optimization problem has been formulated as subject to physical constraints, input torque/force constraints and payload constraints. The mathematical model takes into account the coupled nonlinear equations of manipulator motion. A numerical example shows the efficiency of the proposed procedure.</jats:p>
